apps.name: PIVOT
apps.subtitle: Theme park companion
apps.localizedDescription: Park wait times, ride status, weather observations, planning, shows and Live Activities.
apps.versionDescription:
Waits uses less space between the park card and Current rides, with smaller Recent observed waits controls and less vertical padding. Text keeps its normal size and expands with Dynamic Type.

Map shows current waits when a fresh provider response confirms an unchanged value. Feed status and refresh are available on the map, and refresh continues in full screen and resumes when returning to the app. Failed or expired responses still withhold unverified waits.

versions.localizedDescription:
Waits uses less space between the park card and Current rides, with smaller Recent observed waits controls and less vertical padding. Text keeps its normal size and expands with Dynamic Type.

Map shows current waits when a fresh provider response confirms an unchanged value. Feed status and refresh are available on the map, and refresh continues in full screen and resumes when returning to the app. Failed or expired responses still withhold unverified waits.

Compact ride search, sorting and status filters now share the Waits list with their results.

Unchanged posted waits remain visible when a fresh live response confirms them. Stale or failed feeds still withhold unverified waits.

Removed the artwork badge from thumbnails. Ride details retain truthful illustration credits and reference rights.

Added 73 accepted Florida ride illustrations, bringing the selected coverage to 119 of 145 catalog rides, with 26 remaining gaps. All previously published illustrations are preserved.

Observed-wait dot labels, lowest-wait predictions and best reopening estimates remain included.

Adds 17 accepted Florida ride illustrations for EPCOT, Magic Kingdom and SeaWorld Orlando. All 29 existing illustrations remain, for 46 of 145 Florida catalog rides; 99 remain unfinished. Preserves native ride search, every observed-wait label, lowest-wait predictions, best reopening estimates and readability improvements. Illustrations retain their AI-generated labels and reference attribution. Remaining artwork continues independently.

PIVOT 1.18.0 brings the requested native wait updates together with accepted Florida artwork.

• Search rides by name while keeping current waits and ride status connected.
• See a wait label on every observed chart point, with complete local times.
• See the lowest-wait prediction when fresh, sufficient evidence supports it.
• See the best reopening prediction beside its supported window.
• Read full Radar selections and supporting descriptions at larger text sizes, with clearer chart labels and enlarged hourly views.

This release includes 29 accepted AI-generated Florida ride illustrations across ten parks, including Fyre Drill, Curse of the Werewolf and Hiccup’s Wing Gliders at Epic Universe. Coverage is partial: 29 of 145 Florida catalog rides are covered, with 116 remaining gaps. Other park artwork continues separately. Unaccepted drafts are excluded; generated-artwork labels and source attribution are retained.

Wait and reopening predictions are estimates. Stale, missing or insufficient evidence continues to withhold recommendations. Existing app identity and saved preferences are preserved.

Install as an update to the existing PIVOT app with the same signing identity. Keep the app installed to retain its data. The IPA is unsigned for SideStore to sign; physical-device installation remains untested.

Corrects SideStore update detection by advancing PIVOT to version 1.17.1. This update includes the redesigned park screens and restored PIVOT title from the previous build.

Settings now shows both the app version and build number, making the installed release easy to verify. Map, zoom, full-screen, wait-time and planning controls are retained.

Refreshed park and ride screens across all 32 parks, with the original PIVOT title restored at the top.

A dark layout with rounded cards, park and ride photos where available, clearer wait times, and convenient search, sorting and open/down filters. Park hours, early entry and ride details remain specific to each park.

Native map gestures, zoom and full-screen controls are retained, along with planning, favorites and progress controls. Light/System appearance and large-text layouts remain available.

Refreshed iOS navigation, lists and controls, with a cleaner Plan page.

The park map fills the screen and supports native pinch, pan and zoom controls, with rides, food and show filters. Ride cards show current posted waits, including walk-ons, and clear closed or unavailable states when current data is missing.

Improved large-text layouts, visible Apple map attribution, and preservation of map selection and zoom when entering or leaving full screen.

Expand the park map to full screen and return with Done while keeping your search, filters, selected place, and map position. Tap rides to see current wait times, including walk-ons, or a clear closed or unavailable status when current data is missing or stale. Map pins are more compact while retaining large tap targets.

PIVOT 1.16.0 — A simpler Plan and park maps

Plan now leads with your remaining route and a compact favorites/visit setup. Mark a ride Done or Skip today directly from the route. Fixed stops, full progress, crowd predictions, and offline packs remain available in expandable sections; timing and availability warnings stay visible.

Map replaces Radar in the tab bar. Explore every supported park, filter rides, food, and shows, search places, browse the list, and check fresh ride status. Restaurant pins are locations, not published operating hours. Closures, selected-ride reopening guidance, and park weather remain under More.

This update preserves the existing app identity, saved favorites/progress, manual starts, fixed show stops, offline packs, smart alerts, Live Activities, and the reliability/performance fixes in 1.15.6. The bundled source-backed map catalog was checked October 30. Retired rides remain excluded from active map browsing. Website and backend deployments are separate.

Loading and responsiveness improvements

PIVOT reuses timestamp parsers during live-response decoding and reuses time-label formatters during view updates. Switching parks can start the new park request while an older request finishes. Crowd browsing shares an overlapping selected-park refresh, with its loading indicator preserved.

Freshness rules, the five-second foreground refresh cadence, last-good data, and failure labels remain unchanged. This release includes the Supercharged permanent-retirement removal and EPCOT opening-hours fixes from 1.15.5 and 1.15.4. Saved preferences and app identity are preserved. Backend and website deployment are separate.

Fast & Furious – Supercharged has permanently closed and is removed from active Universal Studios Florida ride listings, temporary-closure forecasts, Radar, plans and active counts. Stale or incorrect provider entries cannot bring it back. Historical records and saved preferences remain intact.

This update preserves PIVOT 1.15.4 opening-hours protection and prior improvements. Native presentation works with the existing server; the separate backend retirement candidate is not deployed by this release. Old saved offline packs remain historical snapshots.

EPCOT opening-hours protection

Scheduled and unverified preopening closures no longer produce breakdown forecasts or overnight closure timers in the iOS app. The verified October 18 openings for Figment, Living with the Land and Gran Fiesta remain separate from park-wide early entry. Missing attraction eligibility is shown as unverified; the scheduled opening time alone never marks a ride open.

Fresh source updates cannot validate forecasts or timers carried over from before the attraction's operating session. Existing saved preferences, plans, app identity and the prior native reliability improvements are preserved.

This release changes native presentation, including its inputs to Radar, planning, local alert processing and app-driven Live Activities. Separate server-side eligibility, evaluation and export changes are prepared for review; installing this IPA does not deploy them or rewrite historical forecasts.

Reopening guidance now shows uncertainty when ride history or current observations cannot support a time. Expired windows stop displaying as upcoming, and saved or failed refreshes cannot keep an exact reopening guess visible.

Weather guidance separates mapped lightning clearance from the park's reopening decision. Unsupported weather times and older push estimates are withheld. Lock Screen guidance expires with its supported window.

You may see fewer numeric forecasts while evidence is limited. This update improves forecast reliability and labeling; a more accurate timing model still needs validation against recent forecast outcomes. Favorites, plans, settings and the existing app identity are preserved.

PIVOT 1.15.1 — Crowd and wait forecasts on Plan

• Find the crowd meter and park/day comparisons beneath Your day on the Plan tab.
• Open Predicted waits on Plan and choose a ride to see its hourly estimates and lowest-wait suggestion.
• Waits and ride information focus on posted waits and recent observations.
• Existing learned history, favorites, plans, app identity, and SideStore compatibility are preserved.

Forecast calculations and learning thresholds are unchanged. Predictions remain preliminary and need sufficient historical observations.

PIVOT 1.15.0 — Predicted waits and park crowds

• A compact crowd meter on Waits uses current posted waits to estimate how busy the park feels.
• Compare supported parks and visit dates, including observed past days and preliminary future estimates.
• Open a ride to see hourly wait estimates and the lowest estimated remaining wait, once enough history is available.
• Forecasts learn from real observations on this device and adjust for today's queue pressure when coverage allows.
• Learning states, confidence labels, missing-hour gaps, and failed-data handling keep unavailable data from looking like a quiet park.
• Existing app identity, saved choices, compact HHN design, and SideStore compatibility are preserved.

Crowds are a wait-based estimate, not attendance or park capacity. Ride forecasts and future crowd ratings need at least three previous observed days. This first model is preliminary and has not been calibrated against real-world outcomes; holidays, events, weather, and operations can change waits. No paid feeds or backend deployment were added.

Fixes HHN house waits disappearing when an unchanged posted wait has an older provider timestamp. Fresh house observations keep valid posted waits, including zero; missing, invalid, future-dated, failed and expired observations remain unavailable. HHN house feed health is independent of regular rides. The app can refresh houses from the same free ThemeParks.wiki provider when the server has omitted waits, with bounded requests and retry backoff. The compact Halloween layout and existing favorites/completion data are preserved. Update the existing PIVOT app with the same SideStore signing identity. Physical SideStore installation remains untested.

Halloween Horror Nights uses a smaller event card and a slim favorites progress strip so houses appear sooner. The moon icon and purple/amber theme remain, with readable event date, hours, ticket notice and Live/Preview/Saved labels. Existing favorites, completion, sorting and previous fixes are preserved. Update the existing PIVOT app using the same SideStore signing identity. Physical SideStore installation remains untested.

Halloween Horror Nights gets a clearer purple-and-amber layout, larger wait numbers, readable house statuses, search, and All houses/Favorites/To do filters. A favorite-house checklist tracks your night; existing favorites, sorting and completed houses are preserved. Preview, saved and unavailable data have distinct labels, and stale or missing waits stay unknown. Large text layouts and touch targets were checked in the iPhone simulator. This native update includes the previous 1.14.1 fixes and preserves the existing app and Live Activity identity. Keep PIVOT installed and update it using the same SideStore signing identity. Physical SideStore installation remains untested.

Saved lightning observations now expire and clearly show saved or unavailable data. Empty or unhealthy ride feeds no longer report that all rides are clear. Failed refresh status stays saved when switching parks, and delayed GPS results no longer override manual park choices. Existing 1.14 features, saved-data keys and the Live Activity extension are preserved. Native update only; backend changes are separate.

privacy.NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription: PIVOT uses your location to select a supported theme park you’re currently visiting.
